hook: Nice used to be an insult. It meant you were ignorant.
modernAnchor: A kind word, a good meal, a pleasant day. We call it nice.
journey: Latin nescius joined ne, not, with scire, to know. It described a person who simply did not know.
Old French turned it into nice, and it reached English in the 1300s meaning foolish or silly.
Over the next few centuries it drifted through shy, fussy and finely detailed, as in a nice distinction.
By the 1700s it meant pleasant, and one of the worst things you could call someone became a compliment.
